items.review_rationale: Read strict global contraction between nonempty metric spaces with one constant q in [0,1) controlling distances for every pair; not simply a local Lipschitz condition.

references.context: For all x,y in X, target distance d_Y(f(x),f(y)) is at most q times source distance d_X(x,y).
One real constant satisfies zero <= q < 1 for every pair, not a pointwise-varying bound.

references.disposition: The two metric spaces are nonempty under the source's explicit convention.

items.review_rationale: Read proper k-coloring of a simple loopless undirected graph as map from vertices to fixed palette with adjacent vertices distinct, k positive and color surjectivity optional.

references.context: Set of k distinct labels available for vertex assignments.
Two vertices joined by an edge in E, which must receive different colors.
For each edge of graph, the two endpoint color labels differ.

references.disposition: A proper k-coloring need not use all k available palette entries.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed left coset gH of subgroup H in G as set of all products gh for h in H, respecting multiplication order and fixed representative g.

references.phrase: left translation by group element g
references.context: Map h↦gh with representative g fixed, using group multiplication on the left.
Set of all group products gh as h ranges over subgroup H.

references.disposition: gH uses multiplication by g on the left and is not automatically equal to Hg for arbitrary subgroup.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed formal real power series about a specified center as infinite indexed coefficients times powers of (x-xi), with convergence deliberately not imposed.

references.phrase: real center xi and coefficients a_n

references.context: Function from nonnegative integers to real coefficients.
Infinite symbolic sum of real coefficient monomial terms centered at xi.

references.phrase: real variable x and shifted powers
references.context: Variable x in R used to form powers of the difference x-xi for n>=0.

references.disposition: Formal series is introduced without claiming its numerical convergence for any value of x.
